body:
Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1523.

## Problem
The sibling `rebuild-and-deploy` (edge job) step in `.woodpecker/acceptance-tests.yml` (lines ~170–188) still uses the pre-#1522 jq filter:

    unhealthy="$(echo "$status_json" | jq -r '(.Allocations // []) as $a
         | (($a | map(.JobVersion // 0) | max) // 0) as $v
         | $a | map(select((.JobVersion // 0) == $v and .ClientStatus != "running")) | length')"

`nomad job status -json` returns a **one-element array** (`[{"Allocations":[...]}]`), not a plain object, so `(.Allocations // [])` exits 5 (`Cannot index array with string "Allocations"`). Confirmed: the array form fed to this filter exits 5 (the same latent bug #1522 fixed only in the `ci.yml` agents path).

Unlike the `ci.yml` step, this edge step carries **neither** the array-unwrap fix **nor** the `|| echo 1` fallback from #1522. With `set -e`, the failing jq in the `unhealthy=$(...)` assignment kills the step on the first health-poll iteration, so the edge deploy step dies with a raw jq exit instead of reporting "edge job not healthy after 120s".

## Fix
Apply the same array-unwrap filter from #1522's `ci.yml` to the edge step so both deploy paths parse `nomad job status -json` identically:
    (if type == "array" then (.[0] // {}) else . end) as $root
    | ($root.Allocations // []) as $a
    | ...
and add the `|| echo 1` fallback so a parse failure reads as "unhealthy" rather than aborting.

Not introduced by PR #1522; reported as pre-existing tech debt for a follow-up.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files
- .woodpecker/acceptance-tests.yml — `rebuild-and-deploy` edge job step (jq health-poll filter, lines ~176-188)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The edge `rebuild-and-deploy` step parses the one-element-array form of `nomad job status -json` (`[{"Allocations":[...]}]`) without the jq filter exiting 5
- [ ] The edge step carries the same array-unwrap filter as `.woodpecker/ci.yml` (from #1522), so both deploy paths parse job status identically
- [ ] A parse failure or empty status reads as "unhealthy" via the `|| echo 1` fallback instead of aborting the step under `set -e` (the step reports "edge job not healthy after 120s")
- [ ] The edge health-poll path exits 0 only when all latest-version allocs report ClientStatus=running
